# creel

**Extract a typed graph from a mess of sources.**

creel is a general, AI-powered **source-to-graph extraction engine**. You give it
(a) **sources** — freeform prose, tables, JSON, PDFs; (b) a **grammar** of the graph
you want — its node-types and edge-types and the typed values they carry; and (c)
**extractors** — pluggable strategies that know how to find each element. creel returns
a clean, auditable, typed **property graph** as a single source of truth, canonically a
JSON graph specification:

```python
extract(sources, graph_spec, extractors) -> graph
```

Everything downstream — persistence, query, graph-RAG, annotation, rendering to
slides/reports — is a *projection* of that one graph.

## Install

```bash
pip install creel                 # core: pydantic, jsonschema, networkx
pip install "creel[query]"        # SQL/JSON query extractors (duckdb, jmespath)
pip install "creel[ingest]"       # file loaders: PDF/DOCX/PPTX via docling, HTML via trafilatura, XLSX via openpyxl
pip install "creel[aix]"          # real LLM extraction/judging/embedding via aix (default)
pip install "creel[anthropic]"    # real LLM extraction via the Anthropic SDK directly
pip install "creel[semantic]"     # LinkML .yaml round-trip + RDF/SHACL validation (pyyaml, linkml, rdflib, pyshacl)
```

LinkML *dict* authoring and RDF-star/Turtle *export* are pure-Python and need no
extra — `[semantic]` only adds `.yaml`-file authoring and downstream validators.
Other extras reserve optional backends: `graphdb` (Neo4j/Oxigraph), `er` (Splink),
`eval` (DeepEval), `ocr` (Tesseract). The headline ones above cover most use;
`pip install "creel[llm]"` is an alias for the default provider (`aix`).

## A first taste

Declare a grammar, extract a graph from prose, validate it, emit canonical JSON:

```python
from creel import (
    GraphSpec,
    NodeType,
    EdgeType,
    AttrSchema,
    EnumDef,
    extract,
    validate_graph,
    to_canonical_json,
)

spec = GraphSpec(
    enums=(EnumDef("Currency", ("USD", "EUR")),),
    node_types=(
        NodeType("donor", attributes=(AttrSchema("name", required=True),)),
        NodeType("project", attributes=(AttrSchema("title", required=True),)),
    ),
    edge_types=(
        EdgeType(
            "funds",
            subject_type="donor",
            object_type="project",
            attributes=(
                AttrSchema("amount", range="integer", required=True, minimum=0),
                AttrSchema("currency", range="Currency", required=True),
            ),
        ),
    ),
)

# Deterministic pattern extractors (no LLM): regex over prose.
bindings = {
    "donor": (
        "regex_node",
        {"pattern": r"Donor:\s*(?P<name>.+)", "id_attribute": "name"},
    ),
    "project": (
        "regex_node",
        {"pattern": r"Project:\s*(?P<title>.+)", "id_attribute": "title"},
    ),
    "funds": (
        "regex_edge",
        {
            "pattern": r"(?P<donor>[\w ]+?) funds (?P<project>[\w ]+?) with (?P<currency>[A-Z]{3}) (?P<amount>\d+)",
            "source_id_template": "donor:{donor}",
            "target_id_template": "project:{project}",
            "casts": {"amount": "int"},
            "exclude_groups": ("donor", "project"),
        },
    ),
}
src = "Donor: Gov X\nProject: Water\nGov X funds Water with USD 1000000"

g = extract(src, spec, bindings, on_missing_binding="skip")
assert validate_graph(g, spec) == []
print(to_canonical_json(g))  # deterministic, git-diffable JSON
print(g.evidence)  # every element traced back to its source span
```

### With a real LLM (schema-as-extractor)

The attribute `description`s become the extraction instruction; the LLM client is
injected (no provider SDK in the core). This block is self-contained:

```python
from creel import GraphSpec, NodeType, AttrSchema, extract
from creel.extract.llm import aix_client

spec = GraphSpec(
    node_types=(
        NodeType(
            "donor",
            description="An entity that provides funding.",
            attributes=(
                AttrSchema(
                    "name", required=True, description="The donor's official name."
                ),
            ),
        ),
    )
)
prose = "Donor: Foundation Alpha (ref 301). Donor: Agency Beta (ref 918)."
g = extract(
    prose,
    spec,
    {"donor": ("llm", {})},
    services={"llm": aix_client()},
    on_missing_binding="skip",
)
```

## Skills (the AI-native interface)

creel is **AI-first**, and that includes how you *learn and drive it*. It ships
**agent skills** — `SKILL.md` cheat-sheets that make Claude (and any `gh skill`-aware
agent: Copilot, Cursor, Codex, Gemini) actually good at using creel, instead of
guessing from docstrings. They install with `pip` (bundled, offline) **or** `gh skill`:

```bash
# All consumer skills ride along with the package:
pip install creel            # creel/data/skills/* is bundled in the wheel

# …or install individually into your agent (cross-agent, pinnable):
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-extract       # the end-to-end workflow
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-grammar       # author a typed GraphSpec
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-bindings      # choose extractor strategies
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-evaluation    # pluggable verifiers (≠ ==)
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-ai            # real LLM extraction
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-projections   # resolve / view / export / trace
# add --agent <copilot|cursor|codex|gemini|claude> to target a host; @vX.Y.Z to pin
```

Once installed, just ask in plain language (“extract a graph from these documents with
creel”, “write a verifier for the amounts”) — the matching skill triggers automatically.
The skills cross-reference each other, so an agent that starts at `creel-extract` is
handed off to `creel-grammar`/`creel-bindings`/`creel-ai`/`creel-evaluation` as needed.
Prefer hand-written API calls? Scroll on — everything below still applies.

## What you get

- **Labeled Property Graph** — attributes (funding amounts, indicator values) live *on
  edges*, which have their own identity; deterministic, git-diffable canonical JSON.
- **Three extractor families** behind one `Extractor` protocol: deterministic
  **pattern/function**, **query** (DuckDB SQL / JMESPath over structured sources), and
  **LLM** (schema-as-extractor, validate-retry, faithfulness gate) — plus **cluster-pass**
  (extract several coupled types in one LLM call).
- **Ingestion** (`ingest()`): route-by-format file loaders (md/csv/json/txt built-in;
  PDF/DOCX/XLSX/HTML via extras).
- **Auditability**: every node/edge/value carries a separable **evidence** record
  (provenance + grounding selector back to the exact source span + confidence). A
  **reverse-trace index** answers “which elements did this passage produce?”, and a
  re-anchoring resolver keeps highlights valid across re-ingestion.
- **Evaluation by pluggable verifiers, not `==`**: `numeric_tolerance`, `set_match`,
  `graph_match` (partial credit), `llm_rubric` (NL-defined, G-Eval), … with a corpus runner.
- **Entity resolution** cascade (normalize → registry → LLM), the **reify** edge↔node
  toggle, **views** (DOT/Mermaid/Cytoscape/tables), and **export** adapters (JGF, GraphML,
  parameterized Cypher, RDF-star).

## Design & docs

The full reasoning lives in the research + design docs: start with the
[synthesis]() (decisions
D1–D15), then the [roadmap](), the
[decision log](), and the
[progress log](). A worked example is in
[`examples/`]().

# _autosummary/creel.annotate.html.md

# creel.annotate

Annotations — the standoff overlay for machine insight AND human coding (D-OP9 / A2).

A single [`Annotation`](_autosummary/creel.annotate.html.md#creel.annotate.Annotation) record serves both directions of authorship: an LLM/
analysis laying an insight over the graph (decision D15) and a human highlighting a
source passage and linking it to a node/edge/category (the manual-“coding” workflow).
They differ only by `motivation` + the provenance agent `kind` — never two
schemas. The overlay is standoff (kept separate from the graph; joined by target).

A [`Selection`](_autosummary/creel.annotate.html.md#creel.annotate.Selection) reifies a region of a source (id + selector) so several
annotations can share one highlighted span. Targets may be a graph element id, an
`(element_id, attribute)` pair (per-attribute, A1), or a [`Selection`](_autosummary/creel.annotate.html.md#creel.annotate.Selection).

### Classes

| [`Annotation`](_autosummary/creel.annotate.html.md#creel.annotate.Annotation)(id, target, body[, motivation, ...])   | A standoff annotation linking a `target` to a `body` with a `motivation`.      |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Selection`](_autosummary/creel.annotate.html.md#creel.annotate.Selection)(id, source_id, selector)                | A reified, shareable selection of a source region (id + a grounding selector). |

### *class* creel.annotate.Annotation(id, target, body, motivation='commenting', provenance=None, confidence=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A standoff annotation linking a `target` to a `body` with a `motivation`.

`target`: an element id (str), an `(element_id, attribute)` tuple, or a
[`Selection`](_autosummary/creel.annotate.html.md#creel.annotate.Selection) (a source span). `body`: a graph-element/category ref (str),
a free-text comment, or any structured insight. `provenance`/`confidence` reuse
the evidence vocabulary; `provenance.attributed_kind` distinguishes a
`software_agent` annotation (machine insight) from a `person` one (human coding).

#### target_element_id()

The graph element id this annotation targets, if any (else `None`).

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### to_dict()

Serialise to a plain, JSON-ready dict.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

# _autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md

# creel.bindings

The extraction-metadata layer: which strategy populates each grammar element.

Per decision D7 this is physically separate from the grammar (`GraphSpec`)
and joined to it on demand ([`creel.join.join()`](_autosummary/creel.join.html.md#creel.join.join)). A binding pairs a taxonomy
element id with either a registered strategy name + pure-data config, or a direct
extractor callable. Keeping this separate means the same grammar can be paired with
different extraction strategies for different source sets — reuse by join, not by
duplication.

Resolution is by a default chain (element-specific → type-default → global
default); unresolved elements fall back to schema-as-extractor at join time.

### Functions

| [`coerce_bindings`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#creel.bindings.coerce_bindings)(extractors)   | Normalise the facade's `extractors` argument into [`ExtractorBindings`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#creel.bindings.ExtractorBindings).   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`ExtractorBinding`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#creel.bindings.ExtractorBinding)(element_id[, strategy, ...])   | Bind one grammar element (or a cluster) to a strategy or a direct callable.                                 |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ExtractorBindings`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#creel.bindings.ExtractorBindings)([bindings])                   | A collection of [`ExtractorBinding`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#creel.bindings.ExtractorBinding), looked up by element id. |

### *class* creel.bindings.ExtractorBinding(element_id, strategy=None, config=<factory>, extractor=None, elements=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Bind one grammar element (or a cluster) to a strategy or a direct callable.

When `elements` is set, this is a **cluster binding** (D-OP8): the extractor is
invoked **once** for the whole set of element ids (one pass over several coupled
types), rather than once per element. `element_id` is then just a label.

#### build()

Instantiate the bound extractor (direct callable wins over a named strategy).

Raises a binding-level [`ValueError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) (naming the element and strategy)
for a malformed config or missing required params, instead of leaking a
`dict`-internals or `__init__` traceback to the caller.

* **Return type:**
  [`Extractor`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.Extractor)

### *class* creel.bindings.ExtractorBindings(bindings=())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A collection of [`ExtractorBinding`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#creel.bindings.ExtractorBinding), looked up by element id.

#### DEFAULT *= '\*'*

element id used for the catch-all / global default binding.

#### for_element(element_id)

Return the binding for `element_id`, else the global default, else `None`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`ExtractorBinding`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#creel.bindings.ExtractorBinding)]

#### *classmethod* from_mapping(mapping)

Build bindings from `{element_id: spec}` where `spec` is flexible.

`spec` may be an [`ExtractorBinding`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#creel.bindings.ExtractorBinding), a `(strategy, config)` tuple,
a `{"strategy": ..., "config": ...}` dict, or a bare extractor callable.

* **Return type:**
  [`ExtractorBindings`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#creel.bindings.ExtractorBindings)

### creel.bindings.coerce_bindings(extractors)

Normalise the facade’s `extractors` argument into [`ExtractorBindings`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#creel.bindings.ExtractorBindings).

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`ExtractorBindings`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#creel.bindings.ExtractorBindings)]


# _autosummary/creel.evaluation.html.md

# creel.evaluation

The evaluation runner — score an extraction corpus with pluggable verifiers.

A corpus case is `{sources, spec, bindings, expected_graph, verifier_overrides?}`
(decision D9). The runner extracts the actual graph and scores it against the
expected one — by default with [`GraphMatch`](_autosummary/creel.verify.graph_match.html.md#creel.verify.graph_match.GraphMatch)
(decomposable partial credit), or with a caller-supplied verifier. Per-attribute
verifiers attach by `(type, attribute)` so most cases need zero per-item config.

This is deliberately thin (decision D11): a function over cases, not a framework.
Roll-ups (per-graph node/edge/attribute scores) come straight from the verdict
`details`; a richer per-type breakdown can be layered on without changing the
contract.

### Functions

| [`evaluate_case`](_autosummary/creel.evaluation.html.md#creel.evaluation.evaluate_case)(case)    | Extract `case.sources` and score the result against `case.expected_graph`.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`evaluate_corpus`](_autosummary/creel.evaluation.html.md#creel.evaluation.evaluate_corpus)(cases) | Evaluate every case and aggregate the results.                               |

### Classes

| [`CaseResult`](_autosummary/creel.evaluation.html.md#creel.evaluation.CaseResult)(name, verdict, actual_graph)        | The outcome of evaluating one case: the verdict + the produced graph.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`CorpusCase`](_autosummary/creel.evaluation.html.md#creel.evaluation.CorpusCase)(name, sources, spec, bindings, ...) | One evaluation item: inputs + how to extract + the expected graph.      |
| [`CorpusResult`](_autosummary/creel.evaluation.html.md#creel.evaluation.CorpusResult)(cases)                            | Aggregate outcome over a corpus.                                        |

# _autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md

# creel.evidence

Evidence — the separable per-element audit record (provenance + grounding + confidence).

Per decision D8, auditability is structural: every extracted node, edge, and value
can carry a small [`Evidence`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.Evidence) record answering three orthogonal questions —
*where from* (provenance), *where exactly* (grounding selectors), and *how sure*
(method-tagged confidence). The record is kept physically separable from the graph
definition (a sidecar keyed by element id) but joinable on demand.

The vocabulary deliberately uses the lightweight cores of W3C PROV / PAV and the
W3C Web Annotation Model as plain JSON (progressive disclosure), so a full
RDF/PROV-O export remains possible later without imposing it now.

### Module Attributes

| [`SOFTWARE_AGENT`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.SOFTWARE_AGENT)   | agent kinds for `Provenance.attributed_kind` (A5) — derive machine vs manual.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`deterministic_evidence`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.deterministic_evidence)(\*, source_id, ...[, ...])   | Build an [`Evidence`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.Evidence) record for a deterministic extraction (confidence 1.0).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`BoundingBoxSelector`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.BoundingBoxSelector)(source_id, page, bbox[, ...])   | Anchor a value to a bounding box on a page (visual grounding for PDF/images).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`CellSelector`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.CellSelector)(source_id, row, column)                | Anchor a value to a table cell (row index + column key).                        |
| [`Confidence`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.Confidence)(method, score[, verified, ...])          | How sure we are, tagged with the *method* (scores are not cross-comparable).    |
| [`Evidence`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.Evidence)(provenance[, grounding, confidence])       | The full audit record for one element: provenance + grounding + confidence.     |
| [`JsonPathSelector`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.JsonPathSelector)(expression[, source_id])           | Anchor a value to a JSON location via a JMESPath/JSONPath-style expression.     |
| [`PageSelector`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.PageSelector)(source_id, page)                       | Anchor a value to a page (coarsest locator for PDF/scanned sources).            |
| [`Provenance`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.Provenance)(derived_from, generated_by[, ...])       | Where an element came from (PROV-lite + PAV as plain JSON keys).                |
| [`TextPositionSelector`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.TextPositionSelector)(start, end[, source_id])       | Anchor by character offsets `[start, end)` within a source.                     |
| [`TextQuoteSelector`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.TextQuoteSelector)(exact[, prefix, suffix])          | Anchor by quoting the exact source text plus a little surrounding context.      |

Coordinates are `[x0, y0, x1, y1]`; `normalized` indicates 0..1 fractions of

# _autosummary/creel.export.html.md

# creel.export

Export adapters — interchange formats for the canonical graph (EPIC 3.4 / 8.4).

Deterministic, **dependency-free** emitters that let the extracted graph flow into the
wider ecosystem without coupling the core to any DB/library (decision D2/D10):

- [`to_jgf()`](_autosummary/creel.export.html.md#creel.export.to_jgf) — JSON Graph Format (the de-facto JSON interchange).
- [`to_graphml()`](_autosummary/creel.export.html.md#creel.export.to_graphml) — GraphML (XML; Gephi/yEd/NetworkX).
- [`to_cypher()`](_autosummary/creel.export.html.md#creel.export.to_cypher) — **parameterized** Cypher statements as *data* (never string
  interpolation — injection-safe; bind the params with a Neo4j driver).
- [`to_turtle()`](_autosummary/creel.export.html.md#creel.export.to_turtle) — RDF-star Turtle; attributes-on-edges become annotations on
  quoted triples (`<< s p o >>`), the lossless LPG↔RDF-star mapping (report R01).

All outputs are id-sorted → stable and git-diffable.

### Functions

| [`to_jgf`](_autosummary/creel.export.html.md#creel.export.to_jgf)(graph)                | Project to JSON Graph Format (v2-style: nodes as an id→object map).          |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`to_graphml`](_autosummary/creel.export.html.md#creel.export.to_graphml)(graph)            | Emit GraphML XML (string attributes; one `<key>` per attribute, id-sorted).  |
| [`to_cypher`](_autosummary/creel.export.html.md#creel.export.to_cypher)(graph)             | Return `(statement, params)` pairs to load the graph into Neo4j safely.      |
| [`to_turtle`](_autosummary/creel.export.html.md#creel.export.to_turtle)(graph, \*[, base]) | Emit RDF-star Turtle; edge attributes annotate quoted triples `<< s p o >>`. |

### creel.export.to_cypher(graph)

Return `(statement, params)` pairs to load the graph into Neo4j safely.

Relationship *types* cannot be parameterized in Cypher, so a generic `:REL` is
used with a `type` property. Bind `params` via the driver — never interpolate.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]]

### creel.export.to_graphml(graph)

Emit GraphML XML (string attributes; one `<key>` per attribute, id-sorted).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### creel.export.to_jgf(graph)

Project to JSON Graph Format (v2-style: nodes as an id→object map).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### creel.export.to_turtle(graph, , base='https://creel.dev/ns/')

Emit RDF-star Turtle; edge attributes annotate quoted triples `<< s p o >>`.

This is the lossless LPG↔RDF-star export (report R01). Caveat: parallel edges of
the same `(source, type, target)` annotate the same quoted triple — distinguish
them downstream by also reifying on the edge id if needed.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/creel.facade.html.md

# creel.facade

The facade: `extract(sources, graph_spec, extractors) -> graph`.

This is creel’s single public entry point and the embodiment of the whole package
(decisions D5/D7/D11). It:

1. normalises the flexible `sources` and `extractors` arguments;
2. equijoins the grammar with the extractor bindings into a runnable plan;
3. maps each resolved extractor over the sources (embarrassingly parallel in
   principle; run sequentially here for determinism and simplicity);
4. assembles the results into a Labeled Property Graph — nodes first, then the
   edges that reference them — attaching each element’s evidence to the separable
   audit sidecar;
5. returns the graph (the single source of truth), with `graph.evidence` and
   `graph.report` carrying the joinable audit/diagnostic layers.

Value-level constraint checking and faithfulness verification are the job of the
verifier subsystem (decision D6), not of the facade.

### Functions

| [`extract`](_autosummary/creel.facade.html.md#creel.facade.extract)(sources, graph_spec[, extractors, ...])   | Read `sources`, populate the graph described by `graph_spec`, return it.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### creel.facade.extract(sources, graph_spec, extractors=None, , cache=None, services=None, on_missing_binding='schema_as_extractor', schema_as_extractor=None, resolve=None)

Read `sources`, populate the graph described by `graph_spec`, return it.

Args (beyond the 3rd, keyword-only):
: cache: a [`Cache`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.Cache) for expensive extractor calls.
  services: injected dependencies (e.g. an LLM client under key `"llm"`).
  on_missing_binding: what to do for grammar elements with no extractor —
  <br/>
  > `"schema_as_extractor"` (use the `schema_as_extractor` factory if
  > available, else skip), `"skip"`, or `"error"`.
  <br/>
  schema_as_extractor: factory `(element_type, spec) -> Extractor` used for
  : unbound elements (provided by the LLM strategy layer; `None` here).
  <br/>
  resolve: an optional [`Resolver`](_autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md#creel.resolve.Resolver). If given, run entity
  : resolution (merge same-entity nodes + remap edges) as a post-extraction
    pass — required for messy multi-source corpora (decision #14).

* **Return type:**
  [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph)
* **Returns:**
  A [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph) (the SSOT). `graph.evidence` maps
  element id → evidence record; `graph.report` holds run diagnostics.


# _autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md

# creel.graph.canonical

Canonical JSON for creel graphs — the deterministic, versioned on-disk truth.

Per decision D4 the canonical form is creel-owned and versioned (`$schema` +
`version`), shapes nodes as an id→object map and edges as objects each with a
**required stable id**, and serialises with sorted keys + id-sorted arrays so that
diffs are one line and round-trips are byte-identical. That determinism is a tested
invariant (`to → from → to` reproduces the exact bytes).

## Public surface

- [`to_canonical_dict()`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.to_canonical_dict) / [`to_canonical_json()`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.to_canonical_json)
- [`from_canonical_dict()`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.from_canonical_dict) / [`from_canonical_json()`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.from_canonical_json)
- [`CANONICAL_SCHEMA_URL`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.CANONICAL_SCHEMA_URL), [`CANONICAL_VERSION`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.CANONICAL_VERSION), [`CANONICAL_GRAPH_SCHEMA`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.CANONICAL_GRAPH_SCHEMA)
- [`validate_canonical()`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.validate_canonical)

### Module Attributes

| [`CANONICAL_SCHEMA_URL`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.CANONICAL_SCHEMA_URL)   | The creel-owned `$schema` identifier for the canonical graph format.     |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`CANONICAL_VERSION`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.CANONICAL_VERSION)      | bump on additive/breaking changes).                                      |
| [`CANONICAL_GRAPH_SCHEMA`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.CANONICAL_GRAPH_SCHEMA) | JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) describing a valid canonical graph document. |

### Functions

|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`from_canonical_json`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.from_canonical_json)(text, \*[, validate])    | Parse canonical JSON `text` into a `Graph` (see [`from_canonical_dict()`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.from_canonical_dict)). |

| [`validate_canonical`](_autosummary/creel.graph.canonical.html.md#creel.graph.canonical.validate_canonical)(data)                     | Validate a canonical document against the format schema.                                                                 |

### creel.graph.canonical.CANONICAL_GRAPH_SCHEMA *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]* *= {'$id': 'https://creel.dev/schema/graph/v1', '$schema': 'https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema', 'additionalProperties': False, 'properties': {'$schema': {'type': 'string'}, 'directed': {'type': 'boolean'}, 'edges': {'items': {'additionalProperties': False, 'properties': {'attributes': {'type': 'object'}, 'id': {'type': 'string'}, 'source': {'type': 'string'}, 'target': {'type': 'string'}, 'type': {'type': 'string'}}, 'required': ['id', 'source', 'target', 'type', 'attributes'], 'type': 'object'}, 'type': 'array'}, 'nodes': {'additionalProperties': {'additionalProperties': False, 'properties': {'attributes': {'type': 'object'}, 'types': {'items': {'type': 'string'}, 'type': 'array'}}, 'required': ['types', 'attributes'], 'type': 'object'}, 'type': 'object'}, 'spec': {'type': ['object', 'null']}, 'version': {'type': 'string'}}, 'required': ['$schema', 'version', 'nodes', 'edges'], 'title': 'creel canonical property graph', 'type': 'object'}*

### *class* creel.graph.Graph

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A labeled property (multi-)graph with stable ids on nodes and edges.

Edge ids are unique across the whole graph (not merely per node pair); this is
what makes the canonical JSON edge-by-id map and per-element provenance possible
(decision D4/D8).

#### add_edge(edge_id, , source, target, type, attributes=None)

Add a typed edge with an explicit, globally-unique id.

Raises `ValueError` if `edge_id` already exists (edge identity is
sacred) or if an endpoint is missing.

* **Return type:**
  [`Edge`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Edge)

#### add_node(node_id, , types=(), attributes=None)

Add (or merge into) a node. Re-adding an id merges types/attributes.

Merging makes extraction idempotent: the same entity surfaced by two
extractors lands on one node rather than duplicating.

* **Return type:**
  [`Node`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Node)

Return the [`Edge`](_autosummary/creel.graph.html.md#creel.graph.Edge) view, or raise `KeyError`.

# _autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md

# creel.graph.model

The in-memory Labeled Property Graph (LPG) — creel’s runtime source of truth.

Per decision D1 the model is an LPG: nodes and edges each have a \*\*stable string
id\*\*, one or more type labels, and a typed attribute bag. Edges are first-class —
they carry their own identity and attributes, so parallel edges of the same type
between the same endpoints (two distinct fundings) stay distinguishable.

[`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph) is a thin, ergonomic wrapper over `networkx.MultiDiGraph`: the
MultiDiGraph gives us multi-edges and per-edge attribute dicts for free, while the
wrapper enforces creel’s invariants (globally-unique edge ids, typed accessors).

### Example

```pycon
>>> g = Graph()
>>> _ = g.add_node("d:gov-x", types=("donor",), attributes={"name": "Government X"})
>>> _ = g.add_node("p:water", types=("project",), attributes={"title": "Water Access"})
>>> _ = g.add_edge("f:1", source="d:gov-x", target="p:water", type="funds",
...                 attributes={"amount": 1_000_000, "currency": "USD"})
>>> _ = g.add_edge("f:2", source="d:gov-x", target="p:water", type="funds",
...                 attributes={"amount": 500_000, "currency": "USD"})
>>> sorted(e.id for e in g.edges_between("d:gov-x", "p:water"))   # parallel edges kept
['f:1', 'f:2']
```

| [`Edge`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Edge)(id, source, target, type[, attributes])   | An immutable view of a graph edge: a first-class, identity-bearing relation.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph)()                                        | A labeled property (multi-)graph with stable ids on nodes and edges.           |

### *class* creel.graph.model.Graph

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A labeled property (multi-)graph with stable ids on nodes and edges.

Edge ids are unique across the whole graph (not merely per node pair); this is
what makes the canonical JSON edge-by-id map and per-element provenance possible
(decision D4/D8).

#### add_edge(edge_id, , source, target, type, attributes=None)

Add a typed edge with an explicit, globally-unique id.

Raises `ValueError` if `edge_id` already exists (edge identity is
sacred) or if an endpoint is missing.

* **Return type:**
  [`Edge`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Edge)

#### add_node(node_id, , types=(), attributes=None)

Add (or merge into) a node. Re-adding an id merges types/attributes.

Merging makes extraction idempotent: the same entity surfaced by two
extractors lands on one node rather than duplicating.

* **Return type:**
  [`Node`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Node)

#### edge(edge_id)

Return the [`Edge`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Edge) view, or raise `KeyError`.

Iterate over all edges.

# _autosummary/creel.html.md

# creel

creel — a general, AI-powered source-to-graph extraction engine.

creel extracts a typed graph from a heterogeneous set of sources (prose, tables,
JSON, schema specs) and emits it as a clean, auditable Labeled Property Graph — the
single source of truth from which downstream persistence, query, annotation, and
rendering are projected.

Conceptually the package is one parameterised facade:

```default
extract(sources, graph_spec, extractors) -> graph
```

It exposes the grammar ([`creel.spec`](_autosummary/creel.spec.html.md#module-creel.spec)), the graph model + canonical JSON
([`creel.graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.html.md#module-creel.graph)), and the `extract` facade with all three extractor families:
deterministic pattern/function ([`creel.extract`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.extract)), query
(`creel.extract.query` — `table_map`/`sql`/`json_query`), and
LLM/schema-as-extractor (`creel.extract.llm`). Around the facade sit the
pluggable verifier subsystem ([`creel.verify`](_autosummary/creel.verify.html.md#module-creel.verify)) and its corpus runner
([`creel.evaluation`](_autosummary/creel.evaluation.html.md#module-creel.evaluation)), file ingestion ([`creel.ingest`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.ingest)), entity resolution
([`creel.resolve`](_autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md#module-creel.resolve)), the reify edge⇄node toggle ([`creel.reify`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.reify)), and the
downstream view/export projections ([`creel.view`](_autosummary/creel.view.html.md#module-creel.view), [`creel.export`](_autosummary/creel.export.html.md#module-creel.export)). See
`misc/docs/design/ROADMAP.md` for the design history.

| [`NormalizedMatch`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.NormalizedMatch)([casefold, strip, collapse_ws])   | Equality after normalising strings (casefold / strip / collapse whitespace).                                                                      |
| [`NumericTolerance`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.NumericTolerance)([abs_tol, rel_tol])              | Compare numbers within an absolute and/or relative tolerance.                                                                                     |
| [`SetMatch`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.SetMatch)([key, threshold])                        | Set-based precision/recall/F1 over (canonicalised) collections.                                                                                   |
| [`SchemaConstraint`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.SchemaConstraint)([spec, predicate, description])  | Property-based check with **no expected value** — validates `actual` itself.                                                                      |
| [`SemanticSimilarity`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.SemanticSimilarity)([threshold])                   | Similarity of free text.                                                                                                                          |
| [`Composite`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.Composite)([components, threshold])                | Weighted combination of named sub-verifiers (promptfoo-style).                                                                                    |
| [`GraphMatch`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.GraphMatch)([spec, attribute_verifiers, ...])      | Score an `actual` [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.Graph) against an `expected` one (partial credit).                              |
| [`LLMRubric`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.LLMRubric)(criterion[, threshold, ...])            | Grade `actual` (optionally against `expected`) by a natural-language criterion.                                                                   |
| [`CorpusCase`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.CorpusCase)(name, sources, spec, bindings, ...)    | One evaluation item: inputs + how to extract + the expected graph.                                                                                |

A standoff annotation linking a `target` to a `body` with a `motivation`.

`target`: an element id (str), an `(element_id, attribute)` tuple, or a

### *class* creel.AttrSchema(name, range='string', required=False, multivalued=False, enum=None, minimum=None, maximum=None, pattern=None, description=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Typed schema for a single attribute (a “leaf” value) of a node or edge.

These follow ordinary schema semantics: a value may be a freeform string or
number (or lists thereof via `multivalued`), or constrained to an `enum`,
bounded by `minimum`/`maximum`, or matched against a `pattern`.

The `description` is load-bearing: it doubles as the default natural-language
instruction for the *schema-as-extractor* and *schema-as-verifier* defaults, so
a usable extraction/verification can often be derived from the grammar alone.

#### NOTE
`minimum`/`maximum` are *value-level* constraints. Per decision D6
they are enforced in the verification pass, not by an LLM decoder’s grammar.

### *class* creel.EdgeType(id, description=None, is_a=None, mixins=(), attributes=(), abstract=False, subject_type=None, object_type=None)

Bases: [`ElementType`](_autosummary/creel.spec.model.html.md#creel.spec.model.ElementType)

An edge-type (a.k.a. link type): first-class, with its own typed attributes.

`subject_type` and `object_type` name the node-types this edge connects
(its endpoints). Edges have their own identity, so two `funds` edges between
the same donor and project (two distinct fundings) are distinguishable.

### *class* creel.ElementType(id, description=None, is_a=None, mixins=(), attributes=(), abstract=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Base for a node-type or edge-type — a position in a recursive taxonomy.

The taxonomy is expressed by `is_a` (single-inheritance parent) plus
`mixins` (multiple inheritance). An element’s *effective* attributes are its
own plus all inherited ones (see [`effective_attributes()`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.effective_attributes)). `id` is an
opaque identifier and may be a dotted path (e.g. `"result.outcome"`) by
convention, but the real hierarchy is the `is_a`/`mixins` graph.

#### attribute(name)

Return this type’s *own* attribute schema named `name` (no inheritance).

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`AttrSchema`](_autosummary/creel.spec.model.html.md#creel.spec.model.AttrSchema)]

#### *property* parents *: [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), ...]*

All direct supertype ids (`is_a` then `mixins`).

### *class* creel.ExtractionContext(element_id, element_type, sources, spec, cache=<factory>, services=<factory>, config=<factory>, element_types=())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Everything an extractor needs to do its job for one grammar element.

`element_id` is the taxonomy id being extracted (a node-type or edge-type id);
`element_type` is its typed schema (whose attribute `description``s drive the
schema-as-extractor default). ``services` carries injected dependencies (an LLM
client, an entity resolver, …) so the core never imports a provider SDK.

#### element_types *: [Sequence](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[ElementType](_autosummary/creel.spec.model.html.md#creel.spec.model.ElementType)]* *= ()*

The cluster of element types this pass covers (D-OP8). Defaults to just
`(element_type,)`; a cluster extractor reads all of them and emits instances
of each in a single LLM pass. `element_id`/`element_type` are the primary
(first) of the cluster, so single-element extractors are unaffected.

### *class* creel.ExtractionPolicy(max_retries=2, self_consistency_samples=1, review_below=0.5, overrides=<factory>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

How the LLM extractor should try, escalate, and flag for review.

* **Parameters:**
  * **max_retries** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – validate-retry attempts for shape/constraint failures.
  * **self_consistency_samples** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – if >1, draw N samples and keep the modal result;
    confidence becomes the agreement fraction (`self_consistency` method).
  * **review_below** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – any element whose confidence score is below this is marked
    `needs_review` (human-in-the-loop gate).
  * **overrides** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`ExtractionPolicy`](_autosummary/creel.policy.html.md#creel.policy.ExtractionPolicy)]) – per element-id or per type-id policies (most specific wins).

#### for_element(element_id, type_id=None)

Resolve the effective policy for an element (element-id → type-id → self).

* **Return type:**
  [`ExtractionPolicy`](_autosummary/creel.policy.html.md#creel.policy.ExtractionPolicy)

### *class* creel.ExtractorBinding(element_id, strategy=None, config=<factory>, extractor=None, elements=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Bind one grammar element (or a cluster) to a strategy or a direct callable.

When `elements` is set, this is a **cluster binding** (D-OP8): the extractor is
invoked **once** for the whole set of element ids (one pass over several coupled
types), rather than once per element. `element_id` is then just a label.

#### build()

Instantiate the bound extractor (direct callable wins over a named strategy).

Raises a binding-level [`ValueError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) (naming the element and strategy)
for a malformed config or missing required params, instead of leaking a
`dict`-internals or `__init__` traceback to the caller.

* **Return type:**
  [`Extractor`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.Extractor)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

element id used for the catch-all / global default binding.

#### for_element(element_id)

#### *classmethod* from_mapping(mapping)

  [`ExtractorBindings`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#creel.bindings.ExtractorBindings)

### *class* creel.Graph

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A labeled property (multi-)graph with stable ids on nodes and edges.

Edge ids are unique across the whole graph (not merely per node pair); this is
what makes the canonical JSON edge-by-id map and per-element provenance possible
(decision D4/D8).

#### add_edge(edge_id, , source, target, type, attributes=None)

Add a typed edge with an explicit, globally-unique id.

Raises `ValueError` if `edge_id` already exists (edge identity is
sacred) or if an endpoint is missing.

* **Return type:**
  [`Edge`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Edge)

#### add_node(node_id, , types=(), attributes=None)

Add (or merge into) a node. Re-adding an id merges types/attributes.

Merging makes extraction idempotent: the same entity surfaced by two
extractors lands on one node rather than duplicating.

  [`Node`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Node)

keyed by attribute name. Unknown `type_id` yields an empty dict.

### creel.extract(sources, graph_spec, extractors=None, , cache=None, services=None, on_missing_binding='schema_as_extractor', schema_as_extractor=None, resolve=None)

Read `sources`, populate the graph described by `graph_spec`, return it.

Args (beyond the 3rd, keyword-only):
: cache: a [`Cache`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.Cache) for expensive extractor calls.
  services: injected dependencies (e.g. an LLM client under key `"llm"`).
  on_missing_binding: what to do for grammar elements with no extractor —
  <br/>
  > `"schema_as_extractor"` (use the `schema_as_extractor` factory if
  > available, else skip), `"skip"`, or `"error"`.
  <br/>
  schema_as_extractor: factory `(element_type, spec) -> Extractor` used for
  : unbound elements (provided by the LLM strategy layer; `None` here).
  <br/>
  resolve: an optional [`Resolver`](_autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md#creel.resolve.Resolver). If given, run entity
  : resolution (merge same-entity nodes + remap edges) as a post-extraction
    pass — required for messy multi-source corpora (decision #14).

* **Return type:**
  [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph)
* **Returns:**
  A [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph) (the SSOT). `graph.evidence` maps
  element id → evidence record; `graph.report` holds run diagnostics.

### creel.from_canonical_dict(data, , validate=True)

Rebuild a [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.Graph) from a canonical dict.

With `validate=True` (default) the document is checked against
`CANONICAL_GRAPH_SCHEMA` before loading, so malformed input fails fast
with a clear error rather than a confusing `KeyError` mid-build.

* **Return type:**
  [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph)

### creel.from_canonical_json(text, , validate=True)

* **Return type:**
  [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph)

Load the file at `path` into a [`Source`](_autosummary/creel.sources.html.md#creel.sources.Source).

The loader is chosen by file extension unless one is passed explicitly. The

### creel.reanchor(selector, text, , hint=None, fuzzy=True)

Re-locate a `TextQuoteSelector` in (possibly changed) `text`.

Strategy (Hypothes.is-style): exact match → disambiguate multiple hits by
prefix/suffix context (and `hint` position) → bounded fuzzy fallback. Returns the
`(start, end)` of the relocated quote, or `None` if it can’t be found. A caller
that resolves only via the fuzzy path should downgrade the element to needs-review.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]

callable can be registered by wrapping it in a factory that ignores config.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Extractor`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.Extractor)]], [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Extractor`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.Extractor)]]

Decorator registering a verifier *factory* under `name`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Verifier`](_autosummary/creel.verify.protocol.html.md#creel.verify.protocol.Verifier)]], [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Verifier`](_autosummary/creel.verify.protocol.html.md#creel.verify.protocol.Verifier)]]

### creel.reify(graph, edge_type, , node_type=None, subject_edge_type=None, object_edge_type=None)

Return a new graph with every `edge_type` edge promoted to a node.

Each promoted edge becomes a node (id = the edge’s id, type `node_type`,
carrying the edge’s attributes), with `source ──subject──▶ node ──object──▶ target`
connector edges. All other nodes/edges (and the evidence sidecar) pass through
unchanged. Other edge-types are untouched, so this is a per-edge-type toggle.

* **Return type:**
  [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph)

### creel.resolve_graph(graph, resolver, , context=None)

Return a new graph with same-entity nodes merged and edges remapped.

Blocking (by node type-tuple) → matching (`resolver.same`) → merging (union-find;
one canonical node per cluster, attributes first-wins) → edge remap. The original
graph is untouched; the result’s `report["merges"]` lists each merge.

* **Return type:**
  [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph)

### creel.schema_description_verifier(element_type, , threshold=0.5)

Build the default `llm_rubric` for an element, seeded from its `description`.

This is the schema-as-verifier default: the same `description` that drives the
schema-as-extractor also becomes the grading criterion.

* **Return type:**
  [`LLMRubric`](_autosummary/creel.verify.rubric.html.md#creel.verify.rubric.LLMRubric)

### creel.set_attribute_evidence(graph, element_id, attribute, evidence)

Attach an evidence record to a specific attribute value (key `(id, attribute)`).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### creel.to_canonical_dict(graph, , spec=None)

Build the canonical dict for `graph` (edges id-sorted; ready to serialise).

If `spec` is given, a lightweight `{"id", "version"}` reference is recorded
so a reader knows which grammar the instance claims to conform to.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### creel.to_canonical_json(graph, , spec=None, indent=2)

Serialise `graph` to canonical JSON text — deterministic and git-diffable.

Keys are sorted and edge arrays are id-sorted, so the same graph always yields
byte-identical output regardless of insertion order.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### creel.to_cypher(graph)

Return `(statement, params)` pairs to load the graph into Neo4j safely.

Relationship *types* cannot be parameterized in Cypher, so a generic `:REL` is
used with a `type` property. Bind `params` via the driver — never interpolate.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]]

### creel.to_cytoscape(graph)

Project to Cytoscape.js `elements` (the reference interactive-view shape).

Node `data` is near-isomorphic to the canonical node object, which is why
Cytoscape is the natural default interactive view (decision D15).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### creel.to_dot(graph, , label_attr=None)

Render the graph as Graphviz DOT (a directed multigraph).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### creel.to_embedding_records(graph)

RAG-readiness: one `{"id","kind","type","text"}` record per element (EPIC 8.1).

`text` is a compact natural-language rendering of the element (type + attributes;
for edges, the relation and its endpoints) suitable for embedding into a vector
index, so the extracted graph flows into graph+vector RAG without coupling.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

### creel.to_graphml(graph)

Emit GraphML XML (string attributes; one `<key>` per attribute, id-sorted).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### creel.to_jgf(graph)

Project to JSON Graph Format (v2-style: nodes as an id→object map).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### creel.to_mermaid(graph, , label_attr=None)

Render the graph as a Mermaid `flowchart` (ids aliased to be Mermaid-safe).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### creel.to_node_edge_records(graph)

Flatten the graph to `{"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}` of plain records.

Each node record is `{"id", "types", **attributes}`; each edge record is
`{"id", "type", "source", "target", **attributes}`. Ideal input for a
DataFrame, a table renderer, or a CSV export.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]]

### creel.to_table(graph, type_id)

Rows for a single node-type *or* edge-type — one record per element.

Returns node rows if `type_id` is a node-type present in the graph, else edge
rows for that edge-type (else an empty list).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

### creel.to_turtle(graph, , base='https://creel.dev/ns/')

Emit RDF-star Turtle; edge attributes annotate quoted triples `<< s p o >>`.

This is the lossless LPG↔RDF-star export (report R01). Caveat: parallel edges of
the same `(source, type, target)` annotate the same quoted triple — distinguish
them downstream by also reifying on the edge id if needed.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### creel.unreify(graph, edge_type, , node_type=None, subject_edge_type=None, object_edge_type=None)

Invert [`reify()`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.reify): collapse well-formed relation-nodes back into edges.

Only nodes of `node_type` that carry **both** a subject and object connector are
collapsed, and only *their* connector edges are removed — so foreign edges that
merely share the connector type, and incomplete/hand-authored nodes of the same
type, are preserved (the toggle is safe on partial/foreign input).

* **Return type:**
  [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph)

### creel.validate_canonical(data)

Validate a canonical document against the format schema.

Raises `jsonschema.ValidationError` if `data` is not a well-formed canonical
graph document.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### creel.validate_graph(graph, spec, , raise_on_error=False)

Return the list of grammar-conformance issues for `graph` under `spec`.

With `raise_on_error=True`, raises [`GraphValidationError`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.GraphValidationError) if any issue
is found instead of returning the list.

# _autosummary/creel.join.html.md

# creel.join

Join the grammar and the extraction-metadata layers into a runnable plan.

Per decision D7 this is a pure equijoin by element id: for every node-type and
edge-type in the `GraphSpec`, find its `ExtractorBinding` (if any) and
resolve the concrete `Extractor`. Elements with no binding fall back to a
`schema_as_extractor` factory when one is supplied (the progressive-disclosure
default), otherwise they are reported as `unbound`.

The result, a [`ResolvedPlan`](_autosummary/creel.join.html.md#creel.join.ResolvedPlan), is what the facade maps over.

### Module Attributes

| [`SchemaAsExtractor`](_autosummary/creel.join.html.md#creel.join.SchemaAsExtractor)   | A factory `(element_type, spec) -> Extractor` used when an element has no binding.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`join`](_autosummary/creel.join.html.md#creel.join.join)(spec, bindings, \*[, schema_as_extractor])   | Equijoin `spec` with `bindings` by element id into a [`ResolvedPlan`](_autosummary/creel.join.html.md#creel.join.ResolvedPlan).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`ResolvedPlan`](_autosummary/creel.join.html.md#creel.join.ResolvedPlan)(steps, unbound)                | The full set of resolved extraction steps plus any unbound element ids.          |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ResolvedStep`](_autosummary/creel.join.html.md#creel.join.ResolvedStep)(element_id, element_type, ...) | One element of the plan: the element(s), the resolved extractor, and the source. |

### *class* creel.join.ResolvedPlan(steps, unbound)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The full set of resolved extraction steps plus any unbound element ids.

### *class* creel.join.ResolvedStep(element_id, element_type, extractor, binding_source, element_types=())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One element of the plan: the element(s), the resolved extractor, and the source.

`element_types` is the cluster this step covers (D-OP8); for an ordinary
per-element step it is just `(element_type,)`.

### creel.join.SchemaAsExtractor

A factory `(element_type, spec) -> Extractor` used when an element has no binding.

alias of `Callable`[[[`ElementType`](_autosummary/creel.spec.model.html.md#creel.spec.model.ElementType), [`GraphSpec`](_autosummary/creel.spec.model.html.md#creel.spec.model.GraphSpec)], [`Extractor`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.Extractor)]

### creel.join.join(spec, bindings, , schema_as_extractor=None)

Equijoin `spec` with `bindings` by element id into a [`ResolvedPlan`](_autosummary/creel.join.html.md#creel.join.ResolvedPlan).

Cluster bindings (`binding.elements`) are resolved first into one multi-element
step each (invoked once). Remaining elements resolve per-element. Node-types are
produced before edge-types so the facade adds nodes before the edges that
reference them.

* **Return type:**
  [`ResolvedPlan`](_autosummary/creel.join.html.md#creel.join.ResolvedPlan)


# _autosummary/creel.policy.html.md

# creel.policy

ExtractionPolicy — the operational policy layer for LLM extraction (decision #13).

This turns a recorded confidence into *action*: how hard to try (validate-retry), when
to spend more for reliability (self-consistency voting on high-value/low-confidence
fields), and when to flag an element for human review (`needs_review`). It is kept
**separate** from the grammar and the bindings (the same separation-of-concerns as
verifiers), and resolved by a chain: per-element → per-type → global default.

The deterministic extractor families ignore it (they are always
`deterministic, score=1.0`); it only bites for the probabilistic LLM extractor.

### Classes

| [`ExtractionPolicy`](_autosummary/creel.policy.html.md#creel.policy.ExtractionPolicy)([max_retries, ...])   | How the LLM extractor should try, escalate, and flag for review.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* creel.policy.ExtractionPolicy(max_retries=2, self_consistency_samples=1, review_below=0.5, overrides=<factory>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

How the LLM extractor should try, escalate, and flag for review.

* **Parameters:**
  * **max_retries** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – validate-retry attempts for shape/constraint failures.
  * **self_consistency_samples** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – if >1, draw N samples and keep the modal result;
    confidence becomes the agreement fraction (`self_consistency` method).
  * **review_below** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – any element whose confidence score is below this is marked
    `needs_review` (human-in-the-loop gate).
  * **overrides** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`ExtractionPolicy`](_autosummary/creel.policy.html.md#creel.policy.ExtractionPolicy)]) – per element-id or per type-id policies (most specific wins).

#### for_element(element_id, type_id=None)

Resolve the effective policy for an element (element-id → type-id → self).

* **Return type:**
  [`ExtractionPolicy`](_autosummary/creel.policy.html.md#creel.policy.ExtractionPolicy)

# creel.render

The renderer contract — the three-layer annotated-graph renderers consume (D15).

creel ships the *contract*, not concrete renderers (those live in consumer packages).
An [`AnnotatedGraph`](_autosummary/creel.render.html.md#creel.render.AnnotatedGraph) is the three layers: the graph (the SSOT), a standoff
[`Annotation`](_autosummary/creel.annotate.html.md#creel.annotate.Annotation) overlay (insights/comments/codings keyed by
target), and optional presentation hints. A [`GraphRenderer`](_autosummary/creel.render.html.md#creel.render.GraphRenderer) turns one into a
[`RenderArtifact`](_autosummary/creel.render.html.md#creel.render.RenderArtifact) (bytes/text + media type).

Use [`creel.view`](_autosummary/creel.view.html.md#module-creel.view) for the dependency-free projections (DOT/Mermaid/Cytoscape/
tables) that concrete renderers build on.

# _autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md

# creel.resolve

Entity resolution — merge nodes that name the same real entity (decision #14 / D-OP8).

Messy multi-source documents (field-written, non-native English, OCR’d) name the
same entity in different ways — “Foundation Alpha” / “Alpha Fnd. (MFA)” /
“the Alpha foundation”. Per the changed decision #14 (report R14 §5), resolution is a
**required**, pluggable cascade — *blocking → matching → merging* — defaulting to
cheap deterministic strategies (exact id → normalize-before-merge → registry) with
hooks for embedding/LLM adjudication.

A [`Resolver`](_autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md#creel.resolve.Resolver) decides whether two nodes are the same entity. [`resolve_graph()`](_autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md#creel.resolve.resolve_graph)
applies one as a post-extraction pass: it blocks by node type, clusters by transitive
sameness (union-find), merges each cluster into one canonical node, and remaps every
edge — non-destructively returning a new graph with a `merges` report.

### Functions

| [`normalize_entity`](_autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md#creel.resolve.normalize_entity)(text)                        | Normalize an entity mention for matching: casefold, strip punctuation/legal/honorific.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`resolve_graph`](_autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md#creel.resolve.resolve_graph)(graph, resolver, \*[, context]) | Return a new graph with same-entity nodes merged and edges remapped.                     |

### Classes

| [`CascadeResolver`](_autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md#creel.resolve.CascadeResolver)(resolvers)        | Try resolvers in order (cheapest first); two nodes match if ANY resolver matches.      |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`LLMResolver`](_autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md#creel.resolve.LLMResolver)(judge[, key])         | Adjudicate hard pairs with an injected judge `(name_a, name_b) -> bool`.               |
| [`NormalizeResolver`](_autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md#creel.resolve.NormalizeResolver)([key, aliases]) | Match by a normalized key attribute (+ an optional alias table).                       |
| [`RegistryResolver`](_autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md#creel.resolve.RegistryResolver)(registry[, key]) | Resolve mentions to canonical ids via an authoritative lookup table (an org registry). |
| [`Resolver`](_autosummary/creel.resolve.html.md#creel.resolve.Resolver)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)      | Decide whether two nodes denote the same real entity.                                  |

### *class* creel.resolve.CascadeResolver(resolvers)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Try resolvers in order (cheapest first); two nodes match if ANY resolver matches.

  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### creel.resolve.normalize_entity(text)

Normalize an entity mention for matching: casefold, strip punctuation/legal/honorific.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### creel.resolve.resolve_graph(graph, resolver, , context=None)

Return a new graph with same-entity nodes merged and edges remapped.

Blocking (by node type-tuple) → matching (`resolver.same`) → merging (union-find;
one canonical node per cluster, attributes first-wins) → edge remap. The original
graph is untouched; the result’s `report["merges"]` lists each merge.

* **Return type:**
  [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph)


# _autosummary/creel.sources.html.md

# creel.sources

Sources — the heterogeneous inputs creel reads.

A [`Source`](_autosummary/creel.sources.html.md#creel.sources.Source) is one unit of input with a stable `id`, a `kind` (so the
right extractor strategy can be routed to it — prose to an LLM, a table to a query
extractor), its `content`, and optionally its own `schema` (when a structured
source carries one, extraction can be made more robust).

A [`SourceBundle`](_autosummary/creel.sources.html.md#creel.sources.SourceBundle) is an addressable collection of sources. [`coerce_sources()`](_autosummary/creel.sources.html.md#creel.sources.coerce_sources)
makes the common cases simple: a bare string becomes one text source, a list of
sources becomes a bundle, etc. (progressive disclosure).

| [`TEXT`](_autosummary/creel.sources.html.md#creel.sources.TEXT)   | Known source kinds.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|

|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`Source`](_autosummary/creel.sources.html.md#creel.sources.Source)(id, content[, kind, schema, metadata])   | One input unit: prose, a table, a JSON document, etc.                                                   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SourceBundle`](_autosummary/creel.sources.html.md#creel.sources.SourceBundle)([sources])                         | An addressable, iterable collection of [`Source`](_autosummary/creel.sources.html.md#creel.sources.Source) objects. |

### *class* creel.spec.AttrSchema(name, range='string', required=False, multivalued=False, enum=None, minimum=None, maximum=None, pattern=None, description=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Typed schema for a single attribute (a “leaf” value) of a node or edge.

These follow ordinary schema semantics: a value may be a freeform string or
number (or lists thereof via `multivalued`), or constrained to an `enum`,
bounded by `minimum`/`maximum`, or matched against a `pattern`.

The `description` is load-bearing: it doubles as the default natural-language
instruction for the *schema-as-extractor* and *schema-as-verifier* defaults, so
a usable extraction/verification can often be derived from the grammar alone.

#### NOTE
`minimum`/`maximum` are *value-level* constraints. Per decision D6
they are enforced in the verification pass, not by an LLM decoder’s grammar.

(its endpoints). Edges have their own identity, so two `funds` edges between
the same donor and project (two distinct fundings) are distinguishable.

### creel.spec.effective_attributes(spec, type_id)

Resolve the full attribute set for a type, including inherited attributes.

Walks `is_a` then `mixins` (depth-first), with a subtype’s own attributes
overriding inherited ones of the same name. Returns an insertion-ordered dict
keyed by attribute name. Unknown `type_id` yields an empty dict.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`AttrSchema`](_autosummary/creel.spec.model.html.md#creel.spec.model.AttrSchema)]

  [`GraphSpec`](_autosummary/creel.spec.model.html.md#creel.spec.model.GraphSpec)

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### creel.spec.validate_graph(graph, spec, , raise_on_error=False)

Return the list of grammar-conformance issues for `graph` under `spec`.

With `raise_on_error=True`, raises [`GraphValidationError`](_autosummary/creel.spec.html.md#creel.spec.GraphValidationError) if any issue
is found instead of returning the list.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`ValidationIssue`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.ValidationIssue)]

### creel.spec.validate_spec(spec)

Check the grammar’s own referential integrity (independent of any instance).

Every edge endpoint type and every `is_a` parent must resolve to a declared
node type — otherwise a spec that references a nonexistent node-type is silently
accepted and never caught. Returns `[]` for a sound grammar.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`ValidationIssue`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.ValidationIssue)]

# _autosummary/creel.spec.linkml.html.md

# creel.spec.linkml

LinkML bridge + schema codegen for the grammar (EPIC 2.4, decision D3).

LinkML is creel’s optional **build-time authoring front-end**, not the runtime SSOT
(the Python [`GraphSpec`](_autosummary/creel.spec.model.html.md#creel.spec.model.GraphSpec) is). This module bridges the two and
generates validation artifacts — all **dependency-free** for the common subset (a
LinkML schema is YAML with `classes` / `attributes` / `enums`), so it is fully
testable without the heavy `linkml` package:

- [`to_linkml()`](_autosummary/creel.spec.linkml.html.md#creel.spec.linkml.to_linkml) — `GraphSpec` → a LinkML schema dict (YAML-able).
- [`load_linkml()`](_autosummary/creel.spec.linkml.html.md#creel.spec.linkml.load_linkml) — a LinkML schema (dict or YAML path) → `GraphSpec`.
- [`generate_json_schema()`](_autosummary/creel.spec.linkml.html.md#creel.spec.linkml.generate_json_schema) — `GraphSpec` → JSON Schema (a `$def` per type,
  with enums/ranges/cardinality) for external validators.
- [`generate_pydantic()`](_autosummary/creel.spec.linkml.html.md#creel.spec.linkml.generate_pydantic) — a Pydantic model per node/edge type for typed access.

Edges are LinkML classes flagged `represents_relationship: true` (the LinkML idiom
for first-class, attribute-bearing relations).

### Functions

| [`to_linkml`](_autosummary/creel.spec.linkml.html.md#creel.spec.linkml.to_linkml)(spec)            | Emit a LinkML schema dict (pass to `yaml.safe_dump` to write a `.yaml`).             |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`load_linkml`](_autosummary/creel.spec.linkml.html.md#creel.spec.linkml.load_linkml)(schema)        | Parse a LinkML schema (dict, or a path to a `.yaml`) into a `GraphSpec`.             |
| [`generate_json_schema`](_autosummary/creel.spec.linkml.html.md#creel.spec.linkml.generate_json_schema)(spec) | Generate a JSON Schema with a `$def` per node/edge type (for external validators).   |
| [`generate_pydantic`](_autosummary/creel.spec.linkml.html.md#creel.spec.linkml.generate_pydantic)(spec)    | Generate one Pydantic v2 model per node/edge type (typed access at the IO boundary). |

### creel.spec.linkml.generate_json_schema(spec)

Generate a JSON Schema with a `$def` per node/edge type (for external validators).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### creel.spec.linkml.generate_pydantic(spec)

Generate one Pydantic v2 model per node/edge type (typed access at the IO boundary).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`type`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#type)]

* **Return type:**
  [`GraphSpec`](_autosummary/creel.spec.model.html.md#creel.spec.model.GraphSpec)

# _autosummary/creel.spec.model.html.md

# creel.spec.model

The grammar layer: a typed description of *what* graph creel should extract.

A [`GraphSpec`](_autosummary/creel.spec.model.html.md#creel.spec.model.GraphSpec) is creel’s **graph-definition** layer and single source of
truth for structure (decision D1/D3/D7). It declares a taxonomy of node-types and
edge-types, each carrying typed attribute schemas. Edges are **first-class**: they
have their own identity and their own typed attributes (funding amounts, indicator
values), and they declare which node-types they connect.

The model is deliberately small, immutable (frozen dataclasses), and free of any
extraction concern — *how* to populate the graph lives in a physically separate
bindings layer joined on demand (see [`creel.bindings`](_autosummary/creel.bindings.html.md#module-creel.bindings)).

### Example

```pycon
>>> spec = GraphSpec(
...     node_types=(
...         NodeType("donor", attributes=(AttrSchema("name"),)),
...         NodeType("project", attributes=(AttrSchema("title"),)),
...     ),
...     edge_types=(
...         EdgeType(
...             "funds", subject_type="donor", object_type="project",
...             attributes=(AttrSchema("amount", range="decimal", minimum=0),),
...         ),
...     ),
... )
>>> spec.node_type("donor").id
'donor'
>>> [a.name for a in spec.edge_type("funds").attributes]
['amount']
```

### creel.spec.model.PRIMITIVE_RANGES *: [frozenset](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]* *= frozenset({'boolean', 'date', 'datetime', 'decimal', 'float', 'integer', 'string'})*

Primitive attribute ranges creel understands out of the box. Anything else is
treated as a reference to a named [`EnumDef`](_autosummary/creel.spec.model.html.md#creel.spec.model.EnumDef) or (later) a node-type id.

### creel.spec.model.effective_attributes(spec, type_id)

Resolve the full attribute set for a type, including inherited attributes.

Walks `is_a` then `mixins` (depth-first), with a subtype’s own attributes
overriding inherited ones of the same name. Returns an insertion-ordered dict
keyed by attribute name. Unknown `type_id` yields an empty dict.

* **Return type:**
