# _autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md

# creel.spec.validate

Validate an instance [`Graph`](_autosummary/creel.graph.model.html.md#creel.graph.model.Graph) against a `GraphSpec`.

This is *structural/shape* validation of an extracted graph against its grammar
(decision D6: the grammar enforces shape; deeper semantic faithfulness is the job
of the verifier subsystem). It checks that node/edge types are declared, that edge
endpoints have conformant node-types, that required attributes are present, and
that attribute values respect their declared range / enum / bounds / pattern.

Use [`validate_graph()`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.validate_graph) to collect issues, or pass `raise_on_error=True` to
raise a [`GraphValidationError`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.GraphValidationError) summarising them.

### Functions

| [`validate_attributes`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.validate_attributes)(attributes, type_id, spec, \*)   | Validate a single element's `attributes` against its type's effective schema.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`validate_graph`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.validate_graph)(graph, spec, \*[, raise_on_error])    | Return the list of grammar-conformance issues for `graph` under `spec`.         |
| [`validate_spec`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.validate_spec)(spec)                                  | Check the grammar's own referential integrity (independent of any instance).    |

### Classes

| [`ValidationIssue`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.ValidationIssue)(element, element_id, code, ...)   | A single grammar-conformance problem found in an instance graph.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Exceptions

| [`GraphValidationError`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.GraphValidationError)(issues)   | Raised by [`validate_graph()`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.validate_graph) when `raise_on_error` and issues exist.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *exception* creel.spec.validate.GraphValidationError(issues)

Bases: [`ValueError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError)

Raised by [`validate_graph()`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.validate_graph) when `raise_on_error` and issues exist.

### *class* creel.spec.validate.ValidationIssue(element, element_id, code, message)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A single grammar-conformance problem found in an instance graph.

### creel.spec.validate.validate_attributes(attributes, type_id, spec, , element_id='')

Validate a single element’s `attributes` against its type’s effective schema.

Used by the LLM extractor’s validate-retry loop (decision D6): the LLM emits
shape-valid JSON, and value-level constraints (enums, ranges, required) are
checked here so the model can be re-asked with the specific failures.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`ValidationIssue`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.ValidationIssue)]

### creel.spec.validate.validate_graph(graph, spec, , raise_on_error=False)

Return the list of grammar-conformance issues for `graph` under `spec`.

With `raise_on_error=True`, raises [`GraphValidationError`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.GraphValidationError) if any issue
is found instead of returning the list.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`ValidationIssue`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.ValidationIssue)]

### creel.spec.validate.validate_spec(spec)

Check the grammar’s own referential integrity (independent of any instance).

Every edge endpoint type and every `is_a` parent must resolve to a declared
node type — otherwise a spec that references a nonexistent node-type is silently
accepted and never caught. Returns `[]` for a sound grammar.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`ValidationIssue`](_autosummary/creel.spec.validate.html.md#creel.spec.validate.ValidationIssue)]


# _autosummary/creel.temporal.html.md

# creel.temporal

Reserved temporal vocabulary (decision #15 / D-OP9 — reserved, not yet enforced).

Temporal modeling is deferred for v1, but the attribute names are **reserved now** so
adding it later (validity intervals, ingestion timestamps, invalidate-don’t-delete)
is purely additive — no schema migration. Extractors/consumers that want to stamp
time should use exactly these keys.

A time-series of indicator readings can be carried today as \*\*parallel `measured_by`
edges\*\* distinguished by `period` (creel’s LPG supports parallel edges natively);
when readings need shared Period/Source/dimension nodes or cross-period merging,
promote them with `creel.reify.reify()` (decision #12).

### Module Attributes

| [`VALID_FROM`](_autosummary/creel.temporal.html.md#creel.temporal.VALID_FROM)   | Start of the validity interval for a fact (valid-time, ISO-8601 string).         |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`VALID_TO`](_autosummary/creel.temporal.html.md#creel.temporal.VALID_TO)     | End of the validity interval (open-ended if absent).                             |
| [`OBSERVED_AT`](_autosummary/creel.temporal.html.md#creel.temporal.OBSERVED_AT)  | When the fact was observed/measured (e.g. an indicator reading's period anchor). |
| [`RECORDED_AT`](_autosummary/creel.temporal.html.md#creel.temporal.RECORDED_AT)  | When creel ingested/recorded the fact (transaction-time).                        |
| [`RESERVED`](_autosummary/creel.temporal.html.md#creel.temporal.RESERVED)     | The reserved temporal attribute names.                                           |

### Functions

|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/creel.trace.html.md

# creel.trace

Bidirectional source↔graph traceability (ADR D-OP9 — A1, A3, A4).

Three additive capabilities that make the extracted graph clickable both ways and
robust to re-ingestion, without changing the canonical graph:

- **A1 — per-attribute grounding.** Attach/read evidence keyed by `(element_id,
  attribute)` (the evidence sidecar already accepts arbitrary keys), so a single
  *property* — not just the node/edge — traces to its source span.
- **A3 — reverse-trace index.** [`TraceIndex`](_autosummary/creel.trace.html.md#creel.trace.TraceIndex) is a rebuildable index over the
  evidence grounding selectors answering “which elements did this source span/cell/
  page produce?” (the inverse of element→source).
- **A4 — anchor robustness.** [`reanchor()`](_autosummary/creel.trace.html.md#creel.trace.reanchor) re-locates a `TextQuoteSelector` after
  the source text changes or is re-OCR’d (quote = system of record; position = hint),
  falling back from exact+context to a bounded fuzzy match.

### Functions

| [`attribute_evidence`](_autosummary/creel.trace.html.md#creel.trace.attribute_evidence)(graph, element_id, attribute)   | Return the per-attribute evidence for `(element_id, attribute)`, or the element-level evidence as a fallback, or `None`.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`reanchor`](_autosummary/creel.trace.html.md#creel.trace.reanchor)(selector, text, \*[, hint, fuzzy])        | Re-locate a `TextQuoteSelector` in (possibly changed) `text`.                                                              |
| [`set_attribute_evidence`](_autosummary/creel.trace.html.md#creel.trace.set_attribute_evidence)(graph, element_id, ...)     | Attach an evidence record to a specific attribute value (key `(id, attribute)`).                                           |
| [`verify_anchor`](_autosummary/creel.trace.html.md#creel.trace.verify_anchor)(selector, text)                      | True if the selector's `exact` quote still occurs verbatim in `text`.                                                      |

### Classes

| [`TraceIndex`](_autosummary/creel.trace.html.md#creel.trace.TraceIndex)(graph)   | A rebuildable index from source locations to the elements grounded there.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* creel.trace.TraceIndex(graph)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A rebuildable index from source locations to the elements grounded there.

Built from a graph’s evidence sidecar. Keys returned are the evidence keys, i.e.
an element id or an `(element_id, attribute)` pair (per-attribute grounding).

#### elements_at(source_id, offset)

Evidence keys whose text span contains `offset` (stabbing query).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

#### elements_in_cell(source_id, row, column)

Evidence keys grounded in table cell `(row, column)`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

#### elements_on_page(source_id, page)

Evidence keys grounded on `page`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

#### elements_overlapping(source_id, start, end)

Evidence keys whose text span overlaps `[start, end)` (range query).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### creel.trace.attribute_evidence(graph, element_id, attribute)

Return the per-attribute evidence for `(element_id, attribute)`, or the
element-level evidence as a fallback, or `None`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Evidence`](_autosummary/creel.evidence.html.md#creel.evidence.Evidence)]

### creel.trace.reanchor(selector, text, , hint=None, fuzzy=True)

Re-locate a `TextQuoteSelector` in (possibly changed) `text`.

Strategy (Hypothes.is-style): exact match → disambiguate multiple hits by
prefix/suffix context (and `hint` position) → bounded fuzzy fallback. Returns the
`(start, end)` of the relocated quote, or `None` if it can’t be found. A caller
that resolves only via the fuzzy path should downgrade the element to needs-review.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]

# _autosummary/creel.verify.graph_match.html.md

# creel.verify.graph_match

`graph_match` — compare a whole extracted graph to an expected one.

Per decision D9 this is **decomposable partial credit**, not all-or-nothing: it
scores nodes and edges with set-based precision/recall/F1 (after canonicalisation)
*and* scores the attributes of matched elements with per-attribute sub-verifiers
(`numeric_tolerance` for amounts, `normalized` for strings, …). The overall
score is a weighted blend, and `details` carries a full breakdown for audit.

Nodes are matched by id (creel’s ids are deterministic, so a correct extraction and
the expected graph share them). Edges are matched by their canonical key
`(type, source, target)` with greedy best-attribute alignment for parallel edges.

### Classes

| [`GraphMatch`](_autosummary/creel.verify.graph_match.html.md#creel.verify.graph_match.GraphMatch)([spec, attribute_verifiers, ...])   | Score an `actual` `Graph` against an `expected` one (partial credit).   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* creel.verify.graph_match.GraphMatch(spec=None, attribute_verifiers=<factory>, node_weight=1.0, edge_weight=1.0, attr_weight=1.0, threshold=0.8)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Score an `actual` `Graph` against an `expected` one (partial credit).

# _autosummary/creel.verify.kinds.html.md

# creel.verify.kinds

The verifier-kind taxonomy — pick the comparison that matches the field’s nature.

These parallel the node/edge/attribute taxonomy (decision D9). The rule: use the
*cheapest verifier that is right* — `exact` only where exactness is correct,
`numeric_tolerance` for amounts/indicator values, `set_match` for unordered
collections, `schema_constraint` for no-gold property checks, `semantic_similarity`
or `llm_rubric` (see [`creel.verify.rubric`](_autosummary/creel.verify.rubric.html.md#module-creel.verify.rubric)) for free text, and `composite`
to weight several together.

Each kind is a callable verifier; each is registered so a binding can name it.
`graph_match` (whole-graph comparison) lives in [`creel.verify.graph_match`](_autosummary/creel.verify.graph_match.html.md#module-creel.verify.graph_match).

# _autosummary/creel.verify.protocol.html.md

# creel.verify.protocol

The verifier contract — the evaluation-time dual of the extractor contract.

The user-emphasized principle (decision D9): comparing an *actual* extraction to an
*expected* one is **not** a hardcoded equality check, but a pluggable
[`Verifier`](_autosummary/creel.verify.protocol.html.md#creel.verify.protocol.Verifier) — and many verifiers are fully defined by natural-language
instructions to an LLM (see [`creel.verify.rubric`](_autosummary/creel.verify.rubric.html.md#module-creel.verify.rubric)).

A [`Verifier`](_autosummary/creel.verify.protocol.html.md#creel.verify.protocol.Verifier) is any callable `(actual, expected, *, context) -> Verdict`,
mirroring the callable [`Extractor`](_autosummary/creel.html.md#creel.Extractor). Every verdict is
a normalised `score` in `[0, 1]` plus a boolean `passed`, an auditable
`reason` (mandatory for LLM judges), and structured `details` (per-component
scores, matched pairs) — the exact shape the whole eval ecosystem converged on.

### Functions

| [`passed_at`](_autosummary/creel.verify.protocol.html.md#creel.verify.protocol.passed_at)(score, threshold)   | Helper: `True` iff `score >= threshold` (used uniformly by all kinds).   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`Verdict`](_autosummary/creel.verify.protocol.html.md#creel.verify.protocol.Verdict)(score, passed[, reason, details])      | The result of a verification: a normalised score plus an audit trail.       |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`VerificationContext`](_autosummary/creel.verify.protocol.html.md#creel.verify.protocol.VerificationContext)([element_type, spec, ...]) | Optional context a verifier may consult (element schema, services, config). |
| [`Verifier`](_autosummary/creel.verify.protocol.html.md#creel.verify.protocol.Verifier)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)                   | A strategy that scores an `actual` value against an `expected` one.         |

### *class* creel.verify.protocol.Verdict(score, passed, reason='', details=<factory>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The result of a verification: a normalised score plus an audit trail.

#### to_dict()

Serialise to a plain dict (reasons retained for audit).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### *class* creel.verify.protocol.VerificationContext(element_type=None, spec=None, services=<factory>, config=<factory>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Optional context a verifier may consult (element schema, services, config).

`services` carries injected dependencies such as an LLM `"judge"` (which
must differ from the extractor model — D9) or an `"embedder"` for semantic
similarity. `element_type`/`spec` let a verifier read the schema (e.g. to
seed an `llm_rubric` from a `description`).

### *class* creel.verify.protocol.Verifier(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

A strategy that scores an `actual` value against an `expected` one.

### creel.verify.protocol.passed_at(score, threshold)

Helper: `True` iff `score >= threshold` (used uniformly by all kinds).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

# _autosummary/creel.verify.rubric.html.md

# creel.verify.rubric

`llm_rubric` — a verifier defined purely by natural-language instructions.

This is the capability the user emphasised: a verifier that is \*fully specified by
instructions to an LLM\*, which judges robustly where a hardcoded comparison cannot
(decision D9). It follows the G-Eval shape — a criterion (optionally expanded into
chain-of-thought eval steps) form-filled into a normalised `[0, 1]` score with a
mandatory `reason`.

The judge model is **injected** via `context.services["judge"]` so the core never
pins a provider SDK, the call is testable with a fake judge, and the \*\*judge can be
held distinct from the extractor model\*\* (self-preference-bias mitigation). The
default rubric is \*seeded from the element’s own schema 

```
``
```

description\`\`\* — the dual
of schema-as-extractor (schema-as-verifier).

A judge is any callable `(prompt: str) -> {"score": float, "reason": str}` (a raw
JSON string with those keys is also accepted).

### Functions

| [`schema_description_verifier`](_autosummary/creel.verify.rubric.html.md#creel.verify.rubric.schema_description_verifier)(element_type, \*)   | Build the default `llm_rubric` for an element, seeded from its `description`.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`LLMRubric`](_autosummary/creel.verify.rubric.html.md#creel.verify.rubric.LLMRubric)(criterion[, threshold, ...])   | Grade `actual` (optionally against `expected`) by a natural-language criterion.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* creel.verify.rubric.LLMRubric(criterion, threshold=0.5, reference_free=False, instructions=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Grade `actual` (optionally against `expected`) by a natural-language criterion.

Set `reference_free=True` to grade `actual` against the criterion alone (no
gold value). `threshold` sets the pass bar.

### creel.verify.rubric.schema_description_verifier(element_type, , threshold=0.5)

Build the default `llm_rubric` for an element, seeded from its `description`.

This is the schema-as-verifier default: the same `description` that drives the
schema-as-extractor also becomes the grading criterion.

* **Return type:**
  [`LLMRubric`](_autosummary/creel.verify.rubric.html.md#creel.verify.rubric.LLMRubric)


# _autosummary/creel.view.html.md

# creel.view

Projections of the graph into views — “one model, many views” (decision D15).

These are *not* renderers; they are deterministic, dependency-free projections of the
canonical graph into the shapes downstream consumers and tools want: flat records
and per-type tables (for DataFrames/reports), DOT and Mermaid (zero-config
visualisation), and Cytoscape.js elements (the reference interactive view). Concrete
renderers (PNG/PPTX/HTML) live in consumer packages on top of these.

All projections are deterministic (nodes/edges id-sorted) so output is stable and
git-diffable.

### Functions

| [`to_cytoscape`](_autosummary/creel.view.html.md#creel.view.to_cytoscape)(graph)                 | Project to Cytoscape.js `elements` (the reference interactive-view shape).      |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`to_dot`](_autosummary/creel.view.html.md#creel.view.to_dot)(graph, \*[, label_attr])     | Render the graph as Graphviz DOT (a directed multigraph).                       |
| [`to_embedding_records`](_autosummary/creel.view.html.md#creel.view.to_embedding_records)(graph)         | RAG-readiness: one `{"id","kind","type","text"}` record per element (EPIC 8.1). |
| [`to_mermaid`](_autosummary/creel.view.html.md#creel.view.to_mermaid)(graph, \*[, label_attr]) | Render the graph as a Mermaid `flowchart` (ids aliased to be Mermaid-safe).     |
| [`to_node_edge_records`](_autosummary/creel.view.html.md#creel.view.to_node_edge_records)(graph)         | Flatten the graph to `{"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}` of plain records.       |
| [`to_table`](_autosummary/creel.view.html.md#creel.view.to_table)(graph, type_id)            | Rows for a single node-type *or* edge-type — one record per element.            |

### creel.view.to_cytoscape(graph)

Project to Cytoscape.js `elements` (the reference interactive-view shape).

Node `data` is near-isomorphic to the canonical node object, which is why
Cytoscape is the natural default interactive view (decision D15).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### creel.view.to_dot(graph, , label_attr=None)

Render the graph as Graphviz DOT (a directed multigraph).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### creel.view.to_embedding_records(graph)

RAG-readiness: one `{"id","kind","type","text"}` record per element (EPIC 8.1).

`text` is a compact natural-language rendering of the element (type + attributes;
for edges, the relation and its endpoints) suitable for embedding into a vector
index, so the extracted graph flows into graph+vector RAG without coupling.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

### creel.view.to_mermaid(graph, , label_attr=None)

Render the graph as a Mermaid `flowchart` (ids aliased to be Mermaid-safe).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### creel.view.to_node_edge_records(graph)

Flatten the graph to `{"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}` of plain records.

Each node record is `{"id", "types", **attributes}`; each edge record is
`{"id", "type", "source", "target", **attributes}`. Ideal input for a
DataFrame, a table renderer, or a CSV export.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]]

### creel.view.to_table(graph, type_id)

Rows for a single node-type *or* edge-type — one record per element.

Returns node rows if `type_id` is a node-type present in the graph, else edge
rows for that edge-type (else an empty list).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`creel` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `creel-ai`

Use a real LLM with creel — wire an injected LLM client, run AI-powered graph extraction, and judge/resolve with a model. Use when the user wants schema-as-extractor extraction, to inject an LLM client (services={‘llm’: aix_client()} or anthropic_client()), the (‘llm’, {}) binding, an LLM judge for llm_rubric verification, LLM entity resolution, self-consistency policy, or to test LLM code with a fake client. Triggers on “use a real LLM with creel”, “extract with an LLM / GPT / Claude”, “schema-as-extractor”, “inject an LLM client”, “aix_client / anthropic_client”, “services={‘llm’:…}”, “the (‘llm’,{}) binding”, “LLM as a judge”, “LLM entity resolution”, “self-consistency voting”, “ExtractionPolicy”, “AI-powered graph extraction”, “fake LLM client for tests”. The LLM is a swappable strategy — no provider SDK lives in creel’s core.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-ai --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`creel/data/skills/creel-ai`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/creel/tree/HEAD/creel/data/skills/creel-ai) (bundled with the pip package).

### `creel-bindings`

Write creel bindings: map each grammar element to an extractor strategy. Use when you need to choose an extractor strategy for a node-type or edge-type, decide pattern vs query vs LLM extraction, write regex_node/regex_edge over prose, or table_map/sql/json_query over structured sources. Covers the binding mental model ({element_id: (strategy, params)} or a bare callable), id templates and casts, endpoint templates for edges, exclude_groups, cluster bindings (cluster_llm), registering a custom extractor strategy, and how unbound elements behave (on_missing_binding). Trigger on: map grammar elements to extractors, route prose to regex and tables to query, bind a funds/measures edge, derive node ids, id_template/id_from, register_extractor a custom strategy, cluster_llm one-pass extraction, on_missing_binding, fix a binding error.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-bindings --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`creel/data/skills/creel-bindings`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/creel/tree/HEAD/creel/data/skills/creel-bindings) (bundled with the pip package).

### `creel-evaluation`

Evaluate / verify a creel extraction — the answer to “is this extraction correct?” is a pluggable Verifier, NOT a hardcoded == . Use when you need to score extraction quality, compare an actual graph to an expected_graph, build a test corpus, or pick the right comparison per attribute. Covers the verifier-kind taxonomy (exact, normalized, numeric_tolerance, set_match, schema_constraint, semantic_similarity, composite), graph_match (decomposable partial credit with a structured mismatch report), and llm_rubric (a verifier defined by a natural-language criterion, graded by an injected LLM judge). Keywords: pluggable Verifier not equality, graph_match partial credit, numeric_tolerance, semantic similarity, natural-language LLM rubric verifier, score extraction quality.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-evaluation --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`creel/data/skills/creel-evaluation`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/creel/tree/HEAD/creel/data/skills/creel-evaluation) (bundled with the pip package).

### `creel-extract`

Extract a typed property graph from messy sources with creel. Use when the user wants to turn prose, tables, JSON, or PDFs/documents into a clean, typed graph — i.e. run extract(), build a property graph, go sources->graph, use the creel facade, or get started with creel. Triggers on “extract a graph from documents”, “build a knowledge/property graph with creel”, “creel quickstart”, “how do I call extract()”, “sources to graph”, “turn this prose/table/JSON into a typed graph”, “ingest a folder of files/PDFs into a graph”, “the one-call creel workflow”. This is the ENTRY/orchestrator skill: it covers the end-to-end extract(sources, graph_spec, extractors) -> graph call, its keyword args (services, on_missing_binding, resolve, cache), and how to read the returned Graph (nodes, edges, evidence, report, validate_graph, to_canonical_json). Hand off to creel-grammar, creel-bindings, creel-ai, creel-evaluation, creel-projections for the deeper pieces.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-extract --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`creel/data/skills/creel-extract`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/creel/tree/HEAD/creel/data/skills/creel-extract) (bundled with the pip package).

### `creel-grammar`

Use when you need to define a creel grammar (a GraphSpec) — the typed schema for the graph you want to extract. Covers declaring node-types and edge-types with AttrSchema attributes; first-class edges that carry their own typed attributes (a funds edge with amount/currency); attribute options (required, range, enum, minimum/maximum, pattern, multivalued, description); reusable EnumDef value-sets and named ranges; inheritance via is_a/abstract/mixins; validating a grammar (validate_spec) and an instance graph (validate_graph); and optionally authoring in LinkML to generate JSON-Schema or Pydantic. Trigger on “define a creel grammar”, “declare node-types and edge-types”, “typed attributes on edges”, “enums/ranges/inheritance for graph extraction”, “schema for graph extraction”, “LinkML authoring”, or “validate a spec”.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-grammar --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`creel/data/skills/creel-grammar`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/creel/tree/HEAD/creel/data/skills/creel-grammar) (bundled with the pip package).

### `creel-projections`

Project/transform a creel graph into everything downstream — persist, query, view, export, annotate are all projections of the one graph, never engine features. Use after you have a Graph and want to clean it up or get it OUT. Covers entity resolution (merge duplicate/same-entity nodes via Normalize/Registry/LLM/Cascade resolvers, the resolve= facade arg, or resolve_graph); the reify/unreify toggle (attributed edge ⇄ relation node when it goes n-ary, losslessly); view projections (to_node_edge_records/to_table/to_dot/to_mermaid/to_cytoscape); export adapters (to_jgf/to_graphml/to_cypher/to_turtle — GraphML, JGF, parameterized Cypher for Neo4j, RDF-star Turtle); the annotate/render contract; and trace (per-attribute grounding, TraceIndex reverse lookup, reanchor to source span). Triggers on “merge duplicate nodes”, “entity resolution”, “reify edge to node”, “view as Mermaid/DOT/Cytoscape”, “export to GraphML/Cypher/RDF/Turtle”, “annotate a graph”, “trace a value to its source span”, “downstream rendering”.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-projections --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`creel/data/skills/creel-projections`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/creel/tree/HEAD/creel/data/skills/creel-projections) (bundled with the pip package).

### `creel-architecture`

Use when working anywhere inside the creel package internals — the source-to-graph extraction engine. Covers the architecture map (layers/modules), the 15 design decisions D1–D15, the key Protocol interfaces, the canonical JSON contract, the two-layer (grammar vs bindings) join, and where each choice is justified in the research. Trigger when adding/changing core modules, wiring the extract() facade, the graph model, the spec/grammar layer, or canonical JSON; or when a design question needs the authoritative answer.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-architecture --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/creel-architecture`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/creel/tree/HEAD/skills/creel-architecture).

### `creel-eval`

Use when building or extending creel’s evaluation/verification subsystem, or when writing tests for extraction. Covers the Verifier Protocol, the verifier-kind taxonomy (exact/normalized/numeric_tolerance/set_match/graph_match/schema_constraint/semantic_similarity/llm_rubric/composite), how an LLM-instruction (G-Eval) verifier is specified and run, the test-corpus layout ({sources, expected_graph, verifier_overrides?}), per-element→per-type→per-graph score roll-up, and the rule that comparisons are pluggable verifiers — NOT hardcoded equality. Trigger on work in creel/verify/, the eval runner, the RBM corpus, or any extraction test.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-eval --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/creel-eval`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/creel/tree/HEAD/skills/creel-eval).

### `creel-extractors`

Use when adding, changing, or wiring an extraction strategy in creel — the pluggable mechanisms that detect and pull a graph element’s value(s) from sources. Covers the Extractor Protocol, the three strategy families (LLM/NL-description, query over structured sources, pattern/function), the registry + entry points, the schema-as-extractor default, the bindings→join→facade flow, and how every extraction attaches an evidence record (provenance + grounding + confidence). Trigger on work in creel/extract/, bindings.py, join.py, facade.py, or evidence.py.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-extractors --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/creel-extractors`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/creel/tree/HEAD/skills/creel-extractors).

### `creel-ingestion`

Use when building or changing creel’s document ingestion layer — turning raw files (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, HTML, Markdown, images) into Sources the extractors consume. Covers the route-by-format + quality-gate escalation strategy, the structure-preserving local default (Docling), grounding/provenance requirements (page/cell/char-span/bbox), the permissive-license discipline, and when to escalate to OCR/VLM or a multimodal model (Claude native PDF + Citations). Trigger on work in creel/ingest/, file loaders, format handling, OCR, or document parsing. Authoritative source: misc/docs/research/13-document-ingestion.md and decision D-OP7.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/creel creel-ingestion --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/creel-ingestion`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/creel/tree/HEAD/skills/creel-ingestion).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install creel`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/creel/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`creel.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/creel/creel.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/creel/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
